name: Zelda's Lullaby
where: Impa, as you leave the Hyrule Castle courtyard after meeting Zelda.
use: Activates Triforce symbols, wakes the Great Fairies and opens the way into Zora Domain and the royal family's doors.
note: Buttons: Y X A Y X A

name: Epona's Song
where: Malon, at Lon Lon Ranch (child).
use: Calls Epona once you are an adult and gets cows to give you Lon Lon Milk if you carry an empty Bottle.
note: Buttons: X Y A X Y A

name: Saria's Song
where: Saria, in the Sacred Grove.
use: Talk to Saria from anywhere for hints, get Darunia dancing (Goron Bracelet) and cheer up the Skull Kid in the Lost Woods.
note: Buttons: R A Y R A Y

name: Sun's Song
where: The royal tomb in Kakariko Graveyard, opened with Zelda's Lullaby.
use: Switches between day and night at once and freezes ReDeads and Gibdos. In the remake, beds also change the time.
note: Buttons: A R X A R X

name: Song of Time
where: Zelda teaches it to you when you pick up the Ocarina of Time from the Castle Town moat.
use: Opens the Door of Time and moves or removes Time Blocks.
note: Buttons: A L R A L R

name: Song of Storms
where: Guru-Guru, in the Kakariko Village windmill (adult).
use: Brings rain, instantly grows Magic Bean plants and opens hidden grottos; played in the windmill as a child, it drains the Kakariko well.
note: Buttons: L R X L R X

name: Minuet of the Forest
where: Sheik, in the Sacred Grove, as an adult.
use: Warps you to the Sacred Grove, by the Forest Temple.
note: Buttons: L X Y A Y A

name: Bolero of Fire
where: Sheik, at the entrance to Death Mountain Crater (adult).
use: Warps you to Death Mountain Crater, by the Fire Temple.
note: Buttons: R L R L A R A R

name: Serenade of Water
where: Sheik, in the Ice Cavern, after you get the Iron Boots.
use: Warps you to Lake Hylia, by the Water Temple.
note: Buttons: L R A A Y

name: Nocturne of Shadow
where: Sheik, in burning Kakariko Village, when you return with the Forest, Fire and Water Medallions.
use: Warps you to Kakariko Graveyard, by the Shadow Temple.
note: Buttons: Y A A L Y A R

name: Requiem of Spirit
where: Sheik, at the Desert Colossus, once you cross the Mirage Desert.
use: Warps you to the Desert Colossus, in front of the Spirit Temple; as a child it is how you get back to the temple.
note: Buttons: L R L A R L

name: Prelude of Light
where: Sheik, in the Temple of Time, when you return with the Forest Medallion.
use: Warps you to the Temple of Time.
note: Buttons: X A X A Y X

name: Scarecrow's Song
where: Bonooru (child) and Pierre (adult), at Lake Hylia.
use: Teach Bonooru eight notes as a child and play them to Pierre as an adult: after that, playing it at certain spots makes Pierre appear as a Hookshot target.
note: Buttons: eight notes of your choice.

name: Kokiri Emerald
where: The Great Deku Tree, after you beat Gohma.
use: The Spiritual Stone of the Forest: one of the three keys to the Door of Time.

name: Goron Ruby
where: Darunia, after you beat King Dodongo.
use: The Spiritual Stone of Fire.

name: Zora Sapphire
where: Princess Ruto, after you beat Barinade.
use: The Spiritual Stone of Water: with all three, head back to the Temple of Time.

name: Light Medallion
where: Rauru, in the Chamber of Sages, after you draw the Master Sword.
use: The first of the six Sages' Medallions.

name: Forest Medallion
where: Saria, after you beat Phantom Ganon.
use: Awakens the Sage of Forest.

name: Fire Medallion
where: Darunia, after you beat Volvagia.
use: Awakens the Sage of Fire.

name: Water Medallion
where: Ruto, after you beat Morpha.
use: Awakens the Sage of Water.

name: Shadow Medallion
where: Impa, after you beat Bongo Bongo.
use: Awakens the Sage of Shadow.

name: Spirit Medallion
where: Nabooru, after you beat Twinrova.
use: Awakens the Sage of Spirit; with all six, the Sages open the way into Ganondorf's Castle.

name: Fairy Ocarina
where: Saria gives it to you as you leave Kokiri Forest.
use: Play songs with D-pad ←. In the remake Link wears it on his belt and moves his fingers with each note.

name: Ocarina of Time
where: Zelda throws it into the Castle Town moat as she flees with Impa.
use: Plays songs and, with the Song of Time, opens the Door of Time. In the remake you can hum songs into the microphone or play a real instrument, hold ZL to see the songs you know and skip the scene after playing one.

name: Bottle
where: The remake has 5: the Cucco Lady (her 7 Cuccos), Talon's Super Cucco game, Ruto's Letter, the Poe Collector (for 5 Big Poes) and a new one from the Castle Town potion shopkeeper, if you help him.
use: Holds potions, fairies, Lon Lon Milk, Blue Fire, Bugs, fish and Poe souls.
note: The first three sources are the original's and are not yet confirmed for the remake.

name: Ruto's Letter
where: Inside a bottle at the bottom of Lake Hylia (child).
use: Show it to King Zora so he lets you through to Zora Fountain; you keep the Bottle afterwards.

name: Gerudo Pass
where: Gerudo's Fortress, when you free the four carpenters.
use: Lets you move freely around Gerudo's Fortress and opens the Gerudo Proving Grounds and horseback archery.

name: Echo Gem
where: The House of Skulltula in Kakariko Village: 20 Gold Skulltula tokens.
use: Equip it: it blinks and vibrates when a Gold Skulltula is near, even one that only comes out at night. It replaces the Stone of Agony, since grottos are now visible.

name: Keaton Mask
where: The Happy Mask Shop in Castle Town, which opens after you show Zelda's Letter in Kakariko Village.
use: Sell it to the guard at the Death Mountain gate. Pay the shop back and it lends you the next mask. In the remake masks also work as an adult (D-pad ↑).
note: Shop prices and order not yet confirmed for the remake.

name: Skull Mask
where: The Happy Mask Shop, once the Keaton Mask is paid for.
use: Sell it to the Skull Kid in the Lost Woods.

name: Spooky Mask
where: The Happy Mask Shop, once the Skull Mask is paid for.
use: Sell it to the boy in Kakariko Graveyard.

name: Bunny Hood
where: The Happy Mask Shop, once the Spooky Mask is paid for.
use: Sell it to the man who jogs around Hyrule Field: he pays whatever fits in your wallet. While you wear it, Stalchildren stay away at night.

name: Mask of Truth
where: The Happy Mask Shop, once you have sold the four masks before it (not yet confirmed for the remake).
use: With it, Gossip Stones tell you their secrets. In the remake it also lets you hear what characters are thinking.

name: Goron Mask
where: The Happy Mask Shop (on loan), after the Mask of Truth.
use: Just for show: some characters react to it.

name: Zora Mask
where: The Happy Mask Shop (on loan), after the Mask of Truth.
use: Just for show: some characters react to it.

name: Gerudo Mask
where: The Happy Mask Shop (on loan), after the Mask of Truth.
use: Just for show: some characters react to it.

name: Retro masks (amiibo)
where: The Young Link and Young Zelda amiibo (2027), with amiibo turned on in the options.
use: Masks based on the original Nintendo 64 models. Other Zelda amiibo give random consumables.

name: Weird Egg
where: Malon, outside Hyrule Castle (child).
use: Wait for it to hatch into the Wake-Up Cucco.

name: Wake-Up Cucco
where: Hatches from the Weird Egg.
use: Wakes Talon, asleep by the castle, so you can head on to the courtyard.

name: Zelda's Letter
where: Princess Zelda, in the castle courtyard.
use: Show it to the guard at the Death Mountain gate to go up; it also opens the Happy Mask Shop.

name: Pocket Egg
where: The Cucco Lady in Kakariko Village (adult).
use: Hatches into the Pocket Cucco the next day.

name: Pocket Cucco
where: Hatches from the Pocket Egg.
use: Use it to wake Talon in his house in Kakariko, then give it back to the Cucco Lady: she gives you Cojiro.

name: Cojiro
where: The Cucco Lady.
use: Take it to the man dozing in the Lost Woods: he gives you the Odd Mushroom.

name: Odd Mushroom
where: The man in the Lost Woods.
use: Take it to the old woman at the Kakariko potion shop before it spoils.
note: The remake's exact time limit is not yet confirmed.

name: Odd Poultice
where: The old woman at the Kakariko potion shop.
use: Go back to the Lost Woods: the man is gone, and the Kokiri who looked after him gives you the Poacher's Saw.

name: Poacher's Saw
where: The Kokiri girl in the Lost Woods.
use: Take it to the head carpenter in Gerudo Valley: he gives you the Broken Goron Sword.

name: Broken Goron Sword
where: The head carpenter in Gerudo Valley.
use: Take it to Biggoron at the summit of Death Mountain: he gives you the Prescription.

name: Prescription
where: Biggoron.
use: Hand it to King Zora (once thawed): he gives you the Eyeball Frog.

name: Eyeball Frog
where: King Zora.
use: Take it to the scientist at the Lake Hylia laboratory before time runs out.
note: The remake's exact time limit is not yet confirmed.

name: Specialty Eye Drops
where: The Lake Hylia laboratory.
use: Take them to Biggoron before they spoil: he gives you the Biggoron Receipt.
note: The remake's exact time limit is not yet confirmed.

name: Biggoron Receipt
where: Biggoron, while he forges the sword.
use: Come back a few in-game days later (beds move time on) and trade it for the Biggoron Sword.

name: Din's Fire
where: A Great Fairy. Per Zelda Wiki, in the remake it is the one on Death Mountain (in the original, the one by Hyrule Castle) (not yet confirmed for the remake).
use: A dome of fire around you: burns webs, lights nearby torches and hurts everything around you. Uses magic.

name: Farore's Wind
where: The Great Fairy at Zora Fountain (not yet confirmed for the remake).
use: Marks a spot in a dungeon so you can warp back to it later. In the remake it returns you to the exact spot, costs 2 magic (was 6) and the point can only be replaced, not removed.

name: Nayru's Love
where: The Great Fairy at the Desert Colossus (not yet confirmed for the remake).
use: A crystal barrier makes you invulnerable for a while. Uses magic.

name: Red Potion
where: The potion shops in Castle Town and Kakariko Village.
use: Restores your hearts.

name: Green Potion
where: Potion shops.
use: Restores your magic.

name: Blue Potion
where: Potion shops.
use: Restores hearts and magic.

name: Lon Lon Milk
where: Talon at Lon Lon Ranch, or any cow you play Epona's Song to.
use: Each bottle holds two drinks that restore hearts.

name: Fairy
where: Fairy fountains, grass, pots and some Gossip Stones; catch it in a Bottle.
use: If you fall, it revives you with several hearts; you can also release it to heal. In the remake you pick them up with A.

name: Magic Beans
where: The salesman by the Zora's River bridge (child); remake price not yet confirmed.
use: Plant them on soft soil as a child; as an adult the flying plant takes you to high places (Pieces of Heart and Skulltulas). The Song of Storms grows them at once.

name: Business Scrub Seed
where: New chests around Hyrule, and amiibo.
use: New in the remake: use it to summon a wandering Business Scrub and buy from him.

name: Blue Fire
where: The blue flames in the Ice Cavern; scoop it up with a Bottle.
use: Melts red ice and thaws King Zora.

name: Bugs
where: Under rocks; catch them in a Bottle.
use: Release them on soft soil and a Gold Skulltula appears (ten are found this way).

name: Fish
where: Ponds and Zora Domain; catch it in a Bottle.
use: Release it in front of Lord Jabu-Jabu so he opens his mouth and lets you in.

name: Deku Seeds
where: Grass, bushes and shops, once you have the Fairy Slingshot.
use: Ammunition for the Fairy Slingshot.

name: Arrows
where: Grass, pots and shops, once you have the Fairy Bow.
use: Ammunition for the Fairy Bow; Fire, Ice and Light Arrows use one arrow plus magic.

name: Gold Rupee
where: The House of Skulltula with all 100 tokens (repeatable) and the Poe Collector with all 10 Big Poes.
use: Worth 200 Rupees.
